rawContent:
Reversing course, about to thanos snap on tinygrad. Shit has lost its way.

Removing:
* CPU/TORCH/LLVM/WEBGPU backends
* Interpreted devices altogether
* All the new things I proposed in the 6000 line tweet

We don't have:
* Sane error messages
* Good enough tests
* Introspection tools

This is the stuff that matters. Small and simple. Nobody cares about a Qualcomm GPU driver and a PTX backend (will pay out this and the WebGL bounties as promised since the work is done, but we aren't going to upstream)

We are targeting three platforms:
* tinybox
* Mac M1+
* comma 3X

Nothing else. We haven't trained ResNet yet, we haven't trained transformers, we have only trained demos. This is what needs to change.

There's deep rot in the Linearizer and in Symbolic that needs to go. We should not be distracted.

In the modern world, you are defined by what you say no to, not what you say yes to. A 5000 line library can train all of MLPerf, and we will prove it.

A bunch of rambling about the tinybox. I don't think there's much value in secrecy.

We have the parts to build 12 boxes and a case that's pretty close to final. Beating back all the PCI-E AER errors was hard, as anyone knows who has tried to build a system like this.

Our BOM cost is around $10k, and we are selling them for $15k. We've put a year of engineering into this, it's a lot harder than it first seemed. "We don't do things because they are easy, but because we thought they would be easy" You are welcome to believe me or not, but unless you are building in huge quantity, you are getting a great deal for $15k.

On the tinygrad side, we trained our first MLPerf qualifying model on a tinybox last week. We are replacing pieces of HIP that aren't up to standard, we replaced the compiler with direct calls to comgr (5x faster compile times) and we are most of the way to replacing the HIP runtime with HSA (one level lower). This is required to make multigpu fast.

The system image shipping with the box will be Ubuntu 22.04. It will only include tinygrad out of the box, but PyTorch and JAX support on AMD have come a long way. and your hardware is your hardware. We make money either way, you are welcome to buy it for any purpose.

The goal of the tiny corp is to commoditize the petaflop, and we believe tinygrad is the best way to do it. Solving problems in software is cheaper than in hardware. tinygrad will elucidate the deep structure of what neural networks are.

We have 583 preorders, and next week we'll place an order for 100 sets of parts. This is $1M in outlay. We will also ship five of the 12 boxes we have to a few early people who I've communicated with. For everyone else, they start shipping in April. The production line started running yesterday.

I have no idea what the preorder conversion rate will be, and don't really want to do something annoying with a second stage preorder. We have funding and can YOLO into the 100 boxes. I trust we'll sell them. First in preorder line will be first offered, and after we e-mail you you'll have a week to pay or lose your spot.

HW specs: 6x 7900XTX full fabric PCI-E 4.0, EPYC 7532, 128 GB RAM, 5x 1TB SN850X SSDs (4 in raid, 1 for boot), 2x 1600W PSUs, and an empty 16x OCP 3.0 slot for networking.

It's a really nice box; I take a lot of pride in building nice things. We will use it as a platform to push the limits of what's possible, you need a standard piece of hardware to do that. Example: that fast Mixtral grok demo can be in theory done on a tinybox (the 6 GPUs have 5.76 TB/s of RAM bandwidth), but the software needs tons of work.

Someday, we want to tape out our own chips. But if you can't build world class software on AMD chip (which is a lot better than the chip you'll make), you shouldn't be messing with expensive tape outs.

We will push the limits of what's possible on this box. The hardware is solid, but the software is a huge journey. I'm excited to be on that journey together with all of you soon to be tinybox owners. To the metal. We will squeeze every last FLOP out of this thing.
